title: The Clay Pot That Gave Birth to a Cup (TE)
summary: Birbal borrows brass pots from a greedy neighbor and returns them with 'baby' cups. When he later borrows a silver cauldron, he announces it 'died.'
full_text:
A greedy neighbor of Birbal named Seth Kundanlal was obsessed with getting something for nothing. Knowing this, Birbal decided to teach him an unforgettable lesson.

One evening, Birbal knocked on the neighbor's door: 'Sethji, I have guests arriving tonight. Could you lend me two large brass cooking pots for twenty-four hours?'

The neighbor reluctantly lent the pots.

The next evening, Birbal returned the two brass pots, along with two tiny, brand-new brass cups nested inside them!

Kundanlal looked confused: 'Birbal, what are these two small cups? They are not mine.'

Birbal smiled innocently: 'Ah, Sethji! It was a miracle! While in my kitchen last night, your two large brass pots gave birth to these two little baby cups! Since the mother pots belong to you, the baby cups belong to you as well!'

The neighbor laughed inside at Birbal's apparent stupidity, greedily pocketed the two free brass cups, and kept the pots.

A week later, Birbal visited the neighbor again: 'Sethji, I am hosting an imperial banquet for fifty nobles. Could you lend me your enormous, antique solid silver cauldron worth five thousand rupees?'

Kundanlal's eyes widened with greed: 'If his brass pots gave birth to brass cups, what will a silver cauldron give birth to? Silver bowls!'

The greedy neighbor gladly handed over his prized silver cauldron.

A week passed. Two weeks passed. Birbal did not return the cauldron.

Unable to wait any longer, Kundanlal marched to Birbal's mansion: 'Birbal! Where is my silver cauldron? And where are the silver babies it gave birth to?'

Birbal stepped out onto his veranda, his face a portrait of profound, weeping grief:

'Alas, Sethji! I bear tragic, heartbreaking news! Last night, after a sudden and violent illness, your beloved silver cauldron passed away! It died, and I had it buried with full honors in the garden!'

The neighbor turned purple with rage: 'Are you completely insane? You liar! You thief! How on earth can a metal silver cauldron die?'

Birbal looked at the shouting merchant with razor-sharp irony:

'Sethji, if a brass pot can give birth to a brass cup, then surely a silver cauldron can get sick and die!

'If you are willing to believe the impossible when it brings you dishonest profit, you must be equally willing to accept the impossible when it brings you loss!'

The dispute was dragged before Emperor Akbar, who laughed until tears filled his eyes, forcing the greedy neighbor to drop his suit and learn that greed invariably swallows its own bait.
